name: FX_Explosion

textures.channels: RGB straight colour (sRGB) + alpha; 8 x 8 frames of 256 px, row by row from the top left

flipbook.blend: alpha with emissive (fire first, smoke after)

source_note: the frames are generated by the build script (seeded, deterministic); the .blend holds the dusk review scene with the mid frame on a card
dresses: explosion, one shot of 64 frames: a fireball swelling to about 2 m, breaking up as it cools, then a rising, thinning ball of smoke
status: source delivered; not imported into Unreal, no effect asset built
known_weaknesses: PARTIAL. A noise-eaten disc that swells, cools and thins by rule: no shock ring, debris, sparks or ground flash, and the smoke does not billow as a simulation would. A flipbook, not an effect: 64 frames of 256 px on one 2048 px atlas for a camera-facing billboard. It is drawn in 2D, so it casts no light, has no depth against the scene (soft-particle fade is engine work), and seen from above it is still a side view. The beauty render is the mid frame on an emissive card at dusk, not a volume. No Niagara system, material or light is authored here.
